57560.recommendedPriorKnowledge: An interest in and familiarity with contemporary critical and cultural theory and its application to the analysis of topical problems and ongoning debates within Humanities scholarship. 59017.name: Moving Images Across Media
59017.recommendedPriorKnowledge: The course will be of special interest to students from Literary and Cultural Analysis, English Literature, Art History, and Media Studies, but also caters to students coming from other humanities and Social Studies disciplines who are interested in questions of representation and media.

59677.name: Banned Books: Literature and the Politics of Censorship

60880.name: Reading in the Digital Age: Close, Deep, Hyper, Machine
60880.recommendedPriorKnowledge: This course explicitly invites students from all scientific and artistic disciplines. It is suitable for seasoned readers who want to learn more about interdisciplinary perspectives on reading, but also for those who want to start reading “seriously” and learn how to do so. All you need for this course is a keen interest in interdisciplinarity, reading and interpretation.

sourceUse: Part B adopted 9 June 2026 supplies the credit rules and Appendix 1 identifies named compulsory units. B4.1 aggregates 42 EC core and a 12 EC philosophy line. The detailed appendix and dated guide name the same upper-year compulsory taught units at 54 EC, including one 6 EC Philosophy of the Humanities and a separate 6 EC workshop. The 12 EC programme-elective total is consistent. Appendix 1 groups 12 EC of programme electives in year two, while the assessment table allows them in years 2–3 and the dated guide and public full-time plan distribute them as 6 EC in each upper year. The dated implementation is shown. The guide’s 42 EC free-choice allocation meets the B4.1 minimum of 30 EC. Both selected electives appear in Appendix 2 and the dated guide, are individually 6 EC and do not duplicate one another. Aesthetics and Politics is first in formal order; Disability, Race, Gender is 12 EC, so the next 6 EC option is Moving Images Across Media. The guide also lists 12 EC Banned Books, which does not fit a single 6 EC slot.

progression.firstYear: The six compulsory credit-bearing modules run from blocks 1–2 foundations through narratology, world literature, contemporary concepts and cultural memory in blocks 2–6. Academic Literacy Test and tutoring have no credits.
progression.secondYear: Positive Humanities binding study advice applies to post-propaedeutic units. The completed first year meets the course requirements for Literary and Cultural Theory Today and the 48 EC threshold for Art, Science, and Technology. Aesthetics and Politics runs in block 1 and is a 6 EC example.
progression.thirdYear: Philosophy of the Humanities is in block 1. Moving Images Across Media and the Thesis Workshop are in block 2. The workshop recommends completion of most core courses, which the first two years supply. The regular 12 EC thesis is in blocks 5–6 after the workshop and requires 120 EC before starting with the supervisor. The first two years total 120 EC. Appendix 1 describes the thesis across semester two while the course guide and assessment table specify the regular final two blocks.
progression.freeElectives: 18 EC in year two and 24 EC in year three remain open. External course participation requires approval. The standard cap on first-year elective credit is 12 EC, with specified minor or language exceptions. A minor, placement or mobility is optional.
